definition: Georgi Gerganov Machine Learning, a C library focused on machine learning
details: Georgi Gerganov Machine Learning, a C library focused on machine learning

explainer.lead: GGML is Georgi Gerganov’s C library for machine learning, closely associated with running language models locally through llama.cpp. Its name also lives on in GGUF, the model-file format that replaced the original GGML format and made quantized models easier to package, share, and load.

tiers.eli5: GGML is a small C-language toolkit named after its maker, Georgi Gerganov, for doing machine-learning calculations. Think of it as a compact workshop for running models on ordinary computers. Its name was also used for an early way of packing model files; newer GGUF files keep the model pieces and instructions together so tools can load them more easily.
tiers.practitioner: GGML is a C machine-learning library; in the llama.cpp ecosystem, the same name also refers to the original model-file format. Current local-inference work generally uses GGUF, with convert_hf_to_gguf.py converting Hugging Face checkpoints and llama-quantize producing integer-quantized variants. Do not treat legacy GGML files and GGUF as interchangeable: the original loader hard-coded hyperparameters and tokenizer details, so architecture or quantization changes could break compatibility.
tiers.paperLevel: GGML (Georgi Gerganov Machine Learning) is a C library for machine learning. In the llama.cpp file-format lineage GGML -> GGMF -> GGJT -> GGUF, the original GGML format was a thin tensor container whose loader hard-coded model hyperparameters and tokenizer information. Consequently, new architectures or quantization schemes generally required loader changes that broke compatibility with existing files; GGUF replaced this with structured key-value metadata.

explainer.example: Start with a Hugging Face checkpoint in safetensors form: convert_hf_to_gguf.py emits an f16 GGUF file, llama-quantize turns it into a Q4_K variant, and Ollama or LM Studio can then load that quantized model for local inference. The lower-precision weights use less memory and may run faster, with some loss of accuracy.

usedIn.name: llama.cpp
usedIn.detail: The project that introduced GGUF and supplies its conversion, quantization, and programmatic file-reading tools.

usedIn.name: Ollama
usedIn.detail: Uses llama.cpp as its inference backend, with models pulled from its registry stored internally as GGUF files.

usedIn.name: Hugging Face
usedIn.detail: Hosts tens of thousands of GGUF checkpoints and provides a metadata viewer, inference-endpoint integration, and JavaScript parser.

usedIn.name: LM Studio
usedIn.detail: Consumes GGUF files directly for local model inference.

explainer.createdBy: The name expands to Georgi Gerganov Machine Learning. The GGUF specification was later formalized through pull request #302 in the ggerganov/ggml repository.
explainer.inAi: The GGML/GGUF ecosystem supports local inference with quantized large language models. GGUF stores tensors, tokenizer data, and loading metadata in one file and can be memory-mapped, including for models larger than available RAM through operating-system paging.
explainer.jsNote: Hugging Face provides a JavaScript parser library for GGUF; this supports the successor file format rather than providing a JavaScript version of the GGML C library.
